### Agent-files version

**An empty file named by the version** (wink, 2026-09-01) because a listing then shows the number
without a read, a bump is a rename git records as one, and the pattern's add-history is the version
log. A one-line file needs a read and a diff for the same answers. A version in AGENTS.md's H1, or
a `## Version` section at its top, was rejected because a heading is an anchor and every bump
would break the links to it. The file is `agent-files-vX.Y.Z` rather than `version-vX.Y.Z` so the
name says what is versioned and does not stutter.

**The `v` spelling** (wink, 2026-09-01) because a bare number after a title's colon could be
anything, and the `v` says "version" in one character, the marker git tags made familiar. Cargo's
output set the rule that keeps it one spelling: bare for a program's own banner (`cargo 1.80.0`),
`v` for a name paired with its version in a line (`Compiling bar v1.0.0`), and the agent-files
version is always the pair.

**The suffix walks in the file name and never in a title** because a rung's title is its ladder
line, which carries no version ([Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a proposal cycle's rungs are told apart by
the bookends while the file says at every commit whether the set is mid-cycle, which is what a copy
taken from a draft bookmark needs to say on its face.

**Proposals bump and adoptions copy** because a proposal is the diff, and the bump is part of it,
while an adoption takes a text that already has its number: the same title in two repos then reads
as the copy and its origin.

**Patch by default, with digit limits** (wink, 2026-09-07) because the earlier rule, patch for a
correction and minor for a rule change, would have moved the minor at nearly every proposal: a set
change is a rule change more often than not, and each is incompatible in the SemVer sense, since an
adopter on the old text and one on the new behave differently until the re-sync. A digit that
moves every time signals nothing, so the agent-files version counts rather than classifies, and the
one-digit patch and two-digit minor are what keep a counter readable at a glance in a file name
and a title.

## The instruction, as it was

The entry in `custom.md > ## Project conventions and overrides`, first in its list, word for word

```
- Lock: at acquaint, before anything else, a session runs `flock -xn .agent-running true` at the

  holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and runs no further command, not even to find the holder. If
  it succeeds, the session starts `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background
  command, leaves it running, and says "Lock taken." If that command exits while the session
  runs, the same sentence and the same stop. A session that already holds one does neither. A
  resumed session is told its holder was stopped with the earlier process, and it runs both
  again before anything else, as at acquaint. This keeps a second session from working in the
  workspace, so two cannot push or amend at once.
```

## Turning it on again

Turning the lock on is putting the entry above back into `custom.md`, in place of the entry that
says the lock is off. What was known and left unsettled when it was turned off:

- The instruction has two faults, and neither had a fix planned:
  - A session that has forgotten it holds the lock probes again at a reacquaint, fails against
    its own holder, and stops as if another session held it.
  - An edit to the instruction reaches only the sessions started after it.
- The lock was to be proposed to the set, and was not. `flock` is a Linux tool and the instruction
  was this project's, and both wanted an answer first.
  - macOS has the `flock` call and does not ship the tool, and Windows has neither.
  - We think the answer is a small `vc-x1` command that takes the lock and holds it, through
    Rust's `File::try_lock`: `flock` on Linux and macOS, `LockFileEx` on Windows, and each system
    drops the lock when the holder dies.
  - That is code in `vc-x1` for the session lock, which the decision of 2026-10-12 was against.
    It weighed races and not other systems.
- The hook that takes the lock in the agent's place is designed and not built ([What a hook
  could do](#what-a-hook-could-do)).

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8

(wink + agent, 2026-10-13) The agent-files name a fetch at an acquaint only, as a `jj git fetch`
and a look, and it is as important that a repo is level at the start of every cycle and when a
cycle lands. The Todo entry picked is "agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8", parked since 2026-10-09 as
one unfinished commit on this cycle's bookmark. Wink asked for the sync rules clean, "as simple
as possible but no simpler".

#### Deliberation

- The rule is one section, [Sync](AGENTS.md#sync), the agent's shape for "as simple as possible":
  the command is written once and the three steps that run it point there.
  - Acquaint looks with `--dry-run`, and Opening and Land sync, each as its first step, wink's
    call, 2026-10-11, on a review of the parked commit.
  - The cycle's bookmark is looked at with `--bookmark` and never synced. The earlier look,
    `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`, read remote refs the fetch had just moved, and a look-only
    sync moves none, so the list would be stale.
  - Land's sync is a clause of the Land paragraph in `jj.md` and not a numbered step, so the
    trapezoid recipe's "Land step 2" keeps its number.
- A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the
  user's to ask for, the agent's addition. Sync holds a repo back since **feat: sync is safe by
  default**, and the parked commit was written before it.
- Started over and not rebased, wink leaving the choice to whichever was simpler.
  - The parked commit's wording was of the sync that rebased a `main` that diverged, and its
    Todo entry had already written it off.
  - Its reasoning is kept in `rationale.md`: why Opening syncs, cycle starts and no oftener,
    "whatever its form", and the bookmark left to a look.
  - The bookmark `agent-filesproposal-v028` was moved to `main` and force-pushed at the opening,
    wink's go, so the parked commit, `2b14ec7e`, change `psuuzqlv`, is findable by that id in a
    clone that fetched it and nowhere on the remote.
- The messages repo's fetch is a line in `custom.md` and out of the set, since the pointer to
  that repo is this project's. Wink's standing permission is the parked commit's, dated
  2026-10-09, and it takes effect with this cycle.
- The rule of the Todo entry "A commit body is an intro and a pointer to the record" is left for
  a proposal of its own, the agent's proposal at the opening, so this one is the sync rules
  alone. The entry said it was part of v0.2.8, and now says what happened.
- The entry's bullet "It stays parked", waiting on whether `zDOING.md` and `zTODO.md` are the
  right files, is lifted by wink's go.
- How a Land recovers from a `main` that moved is left to the first time it happens. We think a
  trapezoid takes the moved `main` as its merge's first parent with no rung rewritten, and a
  single-step commit needs a rebase, which rewrites a published bookmark.
- A cycle first opened this session as "docs: delete stale agent-files proposal v0.2.8", on a
  bookmark of its own, was dropped before any commit when wink chose to complete the proposal.
  Its bookmark was deleted locally and on `origin`.
- A single-step cycle, with a bare version, a bare agent-files version, and no `-dev` name, the
  cycle being documents alone.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, so nothing promotes: `vc-x1 closed` is not a command,
  and the project builds against jj-lib 0.45.

`vc-x1 sync --scope=both` at the three moments a cycle depends on `main`.

- An opening syncs as its first step, before the bookmark.

- `vc-x1 sync --scope=both` run in this cycle reports both repos up to date.

content.text:
Half correct: every project has a `notes/` directory, but what is in it is each project's own, and nothing copies it between members.

# The session lock, and what two sessions in one workspace do

The session lock is the exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` that an agent session holds for as
long as it runs, taken because an instruction in `custom.md` tells the agent to take it. It is
off since 2026-10-13 ([Turned off](#turned-off)), and the instruction is kept here ([The
instruction, as it was](#the-instruction-as-it-was)). This file also holds what was found out
about the lock on 2026-10-12: what Claude Code's hooks could do in the agent's place, and what
happens when two sessions work in one workspace with no lock at all. The lock's own tests, of
2026-10-11, are in the landmark `docs: the session lock is settled as flock`.

The short of it: two sessions lose no data and leave a wrong record, no hook is built, and the
instruction, kept on 2026-10-12, was taken out of `custom.md` the day after.

## What the lock is when it is on

- The agent takes it by hand: `flock -xn .agent-running true` as a probe, then
  `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background command. `vc-x1` has no code that
  touches the lock.
- Nothing releases it. The kernel drops a `flock` when the process holding it exits, and Claude
  Code ends a session's background commands when the session ends.
- It closes no race and needs none closed: a `flock` has one winner whoever asks. A session that
  loses between its probe and its holder learns of it seconds later, when the holder exits, and
  the instruction has it stop then.
- Its weakness is that an agent has to read the instruction and follow it.

# The session lock

An optional rule, off unless a project's [custom.md](../custom.md) turns it on: an agent session
holds an exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` at the workspace root for as long as it runs, so a
second session started in the same workspace stops at its acquaint.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The instruction

Turning the lock on is two edits: this entry goes into
`custom.md > ## Project conventions and overrides`, first in its list and in place of the entry
that says the lock is off, and `/.agent-running` goes into the work-repo's `.gitignore`.

```
- Lock: at acquaint, before anything else, a session runs `flock -xn .agent-running true` at the
  workspace root, alone. If it fails, the session responds with the one sentence "Another session
  holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and runs no further command, not even to find the holder. If
  it succeeds, the session starts `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background
  command, leaves it running, and says "Lock taken." If that command exits while the session
  runs, the same sentence and the same stop. A session that already holds one does neither. A
  resumed session is told its holder was stopped with the earlier process, and it runs both
  again before anything else, as at acquaint. This keeps a second session from working in the
  workspace, so two cannot push or amend at once.
```

Turning it off is putting back the entry that says the lock is off and points here.

## What is known

- Nothing releases the lock. The kernel drops a `flock` when the process holding it exits, and
  the session's background commands end when the session does.
- It closes no race and needs none closed: a `flock` has one winner whoever asks. A session that
  loses between its probe and its holder learns of it seconds later, when the holder exits.
- Its weakness is that an agent has to read the instruction and follow it.
- The instruction has two faults, and neither has a fix:
  - A session that has forgotten it holds the lock probes again at a reacquaint, fails against
    its own holder, and stops as if another session held it.
  - An edit to the instruction reaches only the sessions started after it.
- The tool is Linux's: macOS has the `flock` call and does not ship the tool, and Windows has
  neither.
- Without the lock, two sessions working in one workspace lose no data and leave a wrong record
  (tested 2026-10-12), and one session per workspace is the user's to keep.

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the

and a look, and it is as important that a repo is level at the start of every cycle and when a
cycle lands. The Todo entry picked is "agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8", parked since 2026-10-09 as
one unfinished commit on this cycle's bookmark. Wink asked for the sync rules clean, "as simple
as possible but no simpler".

  the command is written once and the three steps that run it point there.

    call, 2026-10-11, on a review of the parked commit.
  - The cycle's bookmark is looked at with `--bookmark` and never synced. The earlier look,
    `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`, read remote refs the fetch had just moved, and a look-only
    sync moves none, so the list would be stale.
  - Land's sync is a clause of the Land paragraph in `jj.md` and not a numbered step, so the
    trapezoid recipe's "Land step 2" keeps its number.

  user's to ask for, the agent's addition. Sync holds a repo back since **feat: sync is safe by
  default**, and the parked commit was written before it.

  - The parked commit's wording was of the sync that rebased a `main` that diverged, and its
    Todo entry had already written it off.

  commit's, dated 2026-10-09, and it takes effect with this cycle.

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

## Counts

| Landed | Cycle | Files | Lines | Note |

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8

(wink + agent, 2026-10-13) The agent-files name a fetch at an acquaint only, as a `jj git fetch`
and a look, and it is as important that a repo is level at the start of every cycle and when a
cycle lands. The Todo entry picked is "agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8", parked since 2026-10-09 as
one unfinished commit on this cycle's bookmark. Wink asked for the sync rules clean, "as simple
as possible but no simpler".

#### Deliberation

- The rule is one section, [Sync](AGENTS.md#sync), the agent's shape for "as simple as possible":
  the command is written once and the three steps that run it point there.
  - Acquaint looks with `--dry-run`, and Opening and Land sync, each as its first step, wink's
    call, 2026-10-11, on a review of the parked commit.
  - The cycle's bookmark is looked at with `--bookmark` and never synced. The earlier look,
    `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`, read remote refs the fetch had just moved, and a look-only
    sync moves none, so the list would be stale.
  - Land's sync is a clause of the Land paragraph in `jj.md` and not a numbered step, so the
    trapezoid recipe's "Land step 2" keeps its number.
- A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the
  user's to ask for, the agent's addition. Sync holds a repo back since **feat: sync is safe by
  default**, and the parked commit was written before it.
- Started over and not rebased, wink leaving the choice to whichever was simpler.
  - The parked commit's wording was of the sync that rebased a `main` that diverged, and its
    Todo entry had already written it off.
  - Its reasoning is kept in `rationale.md`: why Opening syncs, cycle starts and no oftener,
    "whatever its form", and the bookmark left to a look.
  - The bookmark `agent-filesproposal-v028` was moved to `main` and force-pushed at the opening,
    wink's go, so the parked commit, `2b14ec7e`, change `psuuzqlv`, is findable by that id in a
    clone that fetched it and nowhere on the remote.
- The messages repo's fetch is a line in `custom.md`. Wink's standing permission is the parked
  commit's, dated 2026-10-09, and it takes effect with this cycle.
- An adoption copies `custom.md` and ends on a diff, wink's call: `agent-files copy -c`, then
  `agent-files diff -c` as its last act, in [Agent-files
  version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version).
  - The family's three copies of `custom.md` are the one messaging line, so the file is shared
    in practice, and a copy without `-c` would leave the fetch line behind.
  - An adopter that disagrees with a line drops the `-c`, its prerogative.
  - The other members carry v0.2.5, so their next adoption takes v0.2.6, v0.2.7, and this one in
    one copy, and the versions are not combined here.
- The line saying the session lock is off stays in `custom.md`, wink's call, so every member has
  the option of turning it on. The agent had proposed removing it.
  - The instruction moves into the set, [session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md), wink's
    call, so the family decides on it. A `notes/` directory is every project's and its contents
    are the project's own, so the line's link to `notes/session-lock.md` would be dead in every
    other member's copy.
  - The new file holds the instruction, how to turn it on and off, and what is known of it, and
    names no project. What the tests found stays in `notes/session-lock.md`.
- The rule of the Todo entry "A commit body is an intro and a pointer to the record" is left for
  a proposal of its own, the agent's proposal at the opening, so this one is the sync rules
  alone. The entry said it was part of v0.2.8, and now says what happened.
- The entry's bullet "It stays parked", waiting on whether `zDOING.md` and `zTODO.md` are the
  right files, is lifted by wink's go.
- How a Land recovers from a `main` that moved is left to the first time it happens. We think a
  trapezoid takes the moved `main` as its merge's first parent with no rung rewritten, and a
  single-step commit needs a rebase, which rewrites a published bookmark.
- A cycle first opened this session as "docs: delete stale agent-files proposal v0.2.8", on a
  bookmark of its own, was dropped before any commit when wink chose to complete the proposal.
  Its bookmark was deleted locally and on `origin`.
- A single-step cycle, with a bare version, a bare agent-files version, and no `-dev` name, the
  cycle being documents alone.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, so nothing promotes: `vc-x1 closed` is not a command,
  and the project builds against jj-lib 0.45.

#### Solution

The agent-files gain a section, [Sync](AGENTS.md#sync): both repos are made level by
`vc-x1 sync --scope=both` at the three moments a cycle depends on `main`.

- An acquaint's repo check looks, with `--dry-run`, in place of its `jj git fetch`.
- An opening syncs as its first step, before the bookmark.
- Land syncs as its first step, and a `main` that moved stops it.
- The why of each is in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md#sync).
- The family's `custom.md` adds the messages repo's fetch at an acquaint and at a cycle start.
- An adoption is `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c` and ends on `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c`.
- The session lock's instruction is in the set, off, for the family to decide on.

#### Acceptance check

- [Sync](AGENTS.md#sync) names the command once, and [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint),
  [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), and [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out)'s Land step each point at
  it.
- `rg 'jj git fetch' AGENTS.md custom.md agent-data/` finds only the why of the look in
  `rationale.md`, which names the earlier form.
- `vc-x1 sync --scope=both` run in this cycle reports both repos up to date.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8 (current)

  `main`.

`--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask for.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

# m-9-0 agent-files v0.2.8: sync rules, with v0.2.6 and v0.2.7, in one adoption

vc-x1's set is at v0.2.8 and you carry v0.2.5, so one adoption takes three proposals. The set
is at https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/tree/1139c742b8d4, and the record of v0.2.8 is
https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/1139c742b8d4/zCLOSED.md#agent-filesproposal-v028.

## What it brings

- v0.2.6: the In Progress block's ladder sits below the Deliberation and heads the rung
  subsections.
- v0.2.7: `## Acquaint` in `AGENTS.md`, a session's first steps in order, with a repo check of
  four findings.
- v0.2.8: `## Sync` in `AGENTS.md`. One command, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, is a look at an
  acquaint, with `--dry-run`, and a sync when a cycle opens and when it lands.

## How to adopt

- Install a current `vc-x1` first, 0.84.30 or later. The Sync rule relies on `sync --dry-run` and
  on sync holding a repo back, and an older binary rebases.
- Copy with `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c ../vc-x1`, and end the adoption on
  `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c ../vc-x1`, which exits zero when the copies are the same. This is
  the new rule in `versioning.md`.
- The `-c` takes `custom.md`, which the three of us hold as the same file. Drop it from both
  commands if you disagree with a line, which is your prerogative.

## Two lines in custom.md to decide on

- The messages repo's fetch: a session does this README's Fetch action at an acquaint and at
  every cycle start, wink's permission standing.
- The session lock is off. Its instruction is a new file of the set,
  `agent-data/session-lock.md`, with how to turn it on and what is known of it. Whether the
  family turns it on is yours to say.

Reply with what you take and what you do not.
